context.analysis:
## Overview
[System Processes real-time card-not-present payment authorizations in AWS for fraud screening and provides an analyst review interface.]
[Core purpose is to deliver sub-50ms fraud decisions while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.]

## Key Elements
- **Payment Gateway / Acquirer**: External system sending transaction requests.
- **Tokenization Vault**: External system resolving card tokens for secure data handling.
- **Identity Provider (IdP)**: External system managing OIDC/SAML authentication and MFA.
- **Fraud Screening Engine (System-to-Be)**: AWS-hosted containerized system for scoring and case management.
- **WORM Compliance Storage**: External AWS S3 storage for 7-year audit logs.

## Relationships
- **Payment Gateway to Fraud Screening Engine**: Sends real-time payment events via HTTPS/gRPC with mTLS.
- **Fraud Screening Engine to Tokenization Vault**: Resolves tokens via HTTPS REST API.
- **Fraud Screening Engine to Identity Provider**: Authenticates analysts using OIDC/SAML.
- **Fraud Screening Engine to WORM Compliance Storage**: Sends cryptographically signed decision logs via AWS S3 APIs.

## Technology Stack
- **AWS ECS on Fargate**: Container orchestration chosen to avoid serverless cold starts and stay within the €25k budget.
- **AWS KMS**: Manages customer-managed keys (CMK) and asymmetric signing for tamper-evident R-06 audit logs and data encryption.
- **Terraform**: Infrastructure as Code tool used by the 3-engineer team to automate deployments via GitOps.
- **AWS Secrets Manager**: Eliminates hardcoded credentials to meet PCI-DSS Level 1 mandates.

## Rationale
[AWS managed services and containerization on Fargate provide high availability and meet the strict <50ms P99 latency within budget constraints.]
[A containerized GitOps approach and immutable storage enable a 3-engineer team to maintain PCI-DSS compliance and 7-year auditability effortlessly.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates card-not-present transactions for a mid-size payment processor and provides case management for fraud analysts. Its core purpose is to screen authorizations in real time while ensuring strict compliance, auditability, and uninterrupted checkout flows.]

## Key Elements
- Cardholder / End Customer
- Fraud Analyst
- Risk / Fraud Manager
- AWS API Gateway / ALB
- Scoring Engine (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management API (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Rule & Model Registry (Amazon S3)
- Amazon DynamoDB
- Amazon Kinesis Data Streams & AWS S3 Firehose
- WORM Compliance Storage (Amazon S3 with Object Lock)
- External Identity Provider (IdP) & Tokenization Vault

## Relationships
- Cardholder to AWS API Gateway via HTTPS/JSON
- API Gateway to Scoring Engine via mTLS / gRPC
- Scoring Engine to Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon Kinesis Data Streams via AWS SDK
- Scoring Engine to Amazon S3 (Rule & Model Registry) via HTTPS
- Fraud Analyst to Case Management API via HTTPS/OAuth2
- Scoring Engine and Case Management to WORM Compliance Storage via S3 Firehose

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Provides container orchestration without Kubernetes operational overhead to fit the 3-person team limit and €25k budget.
- Go or Rust: Implements the low-latency Scoring Engine to guarantee <50ms P99 decision latency.
- Amazon DynamoDB: Delivers low-latency storage for feature stores and case data.
- Amazon Kinesis Data Streams: Handles high-throughput, durable audit log streaming.
- Amazon S3 Object Lock: Ensures tamper-evident WORM compliance storage for 7-year audit retention.
- AWS KMS: Implements envelope encryption, secret management, and cryptographic rule artifact signatures.

## Rationale
[This architecture uses managed AWS services and local in-memory caching to achieve ultra-low latency and PCI-DSS compliance within tight operational constraints. It minimizes infrastructure complexity to support a three-engineer team within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.]

AWS API Gateway / ALB.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in under 50ms and manages cases for fraud analysts. It operates under strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 7-year auditability constraint within a €25,000 monthly AWS budget.

## Key Elements
* Payment Gateway / Acquirer (External Partner)
* Tokenization Vault (External System)
* AWS API Gateway / ALB (Perimeter Security & Routing Container)
* Scoring Engine (Go/Rust, AWS ECS Fargate Container)
* Case Management API (AWS ECS Fargate Container)
* Rule & Model Registry (Amazon S3)
* Amazon DynamoDB & WORM Compliance Storage
* Fraud Analysts & Fraud Engineers (Internal Users)

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway / Acquirer -> AWS API Gateway / ALB: Sends pre-tokenized authorization requests [mTLS / HTTPS]
* AWS API Gateway / ALB -> Scoring Engine: Forwards scoring requests [gRPC / mTLS]
* Scoring Engine -> Rule & Model Registry: Fetches rules and models [HTTPS / S3 API]
* Scoring Engine -> WORM Compliance Storage: Stores tamper-evident audit logs [HTTPS]
* Fraud Analysts -> Case Management API: Reviews flagged cases [HTTPS / JSON]

## Technology Stack
* AWS API Gateway & ALB with AWS WAF v2: Perimeter security, mTLS termination, and JWT validation for low latency
* AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration matching a 3-engineer operational capacity
* Go / Rust: High-performance backend runtime for sub-50ms P99 latency requirements
* Amazon DynamoDB: Low-latency storage for real-time case management
* Terraform: Infrastructure as Code for automated, budget-compliant deployments

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team while easily scaling to 3,000 requests per second. Strict perimeter mTLS, tokenization offloading, and immutable audit logs guarantee PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability within the €25k budget.

Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud under strict latency and compliance constraints. It evaluates transactions in real time and provides case management tools for fraud analysts.

## Key Elements
- **API Router & Validator (Go):** Validates incoming gRPC payloads and enforces schema integrity.
- **Feature Assembler (Go):** Queries DynamoDB for user and card velocity features with parallelized execution.
- **Inference & Rules Evaluator (Rust):** Executes compiled machine learning models and dynamic rule sets concurrently.
- **Model Loader Component (Rust):** Handles S3 event notifications, cryptographic signature verification, and atomic in-memory model hot-swapping.
- **Audit Dispatcher (Go):** Asynchronously emits cryptographically signed, tamper-evident audit records.
- **External Dependencies:** AWS API Gateway / ALB, Amazon DynamoDB, Rule & Model Registry (Amazon S3), Amazon Kinesis Data Streams / AWS S3 Firehose, WORM Compliance Storage.

## Relationships
- **AWS API Gateway / ALB -> API Router & Validator:** Routes incoming authorization requests via [mTLS / gRPC].
- **Feature Assembler -> Amazon DynamoDB:** Reads and writes feature stores and transaction data using [AWS SDK].
- **Model Loader Component -> Rule & Model Registry:** Receives S3 event notifications and fetches model artifacts via [HTTPS / AWS SDK].
- **Audit Dispatcher -> Amazon Kinesis Data Streams & AWS S3 Firehose:** Streams audit logs via [AWS SDK].
- **Audit Dispatcher -> WORM Compliance Storage:** Persists immutable compliance logs via [S3 Firehose].

## Technology Stack
- **Go & Rust (AWS ECS Fargate):** Go handles concurrent API routing and I/O tasks, while Rust guarantees zero garbage-collection pauses for sub-50ms P99 latency targets.
- **Amazon DynamoDB:** Stores feature stores and transaction data with AWS KMS encryption for low-latency lookups.
- **Amazon S3 & AWS KMS:** Stores model artifacts and audit data with cryptographic signature verification and KMS encryption.
- **Amazon Kinesis Data Streams & AWS S3 Firehose:** Streams immutable, cryptographically hashed audit logs to WORM storage.
- **OpenTelemetry & AWS CloudWatch:** Provides structured metrics and distributed tracing for operational observability within budget constraints.

## Rationale
This architecture combines Go and Rust on AWS ECS Fargate to predictably meet the strict sub-50ms P99 latency requirement at 3,000 TPS within a fixed 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Furthermore, event-driven cryptographic model loading and tamper-evident audit logging satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability mandates.

Case Management API.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening engine for card-not-present transactions, paired with a Case Management API that empowers analysts to review suspicious payments. It ensures PCI-DSS compliance, 7-year tamper-evident auditability, and sub-50ms latency within a 25,000 EUR/month AWS budget.]

## Key Elements
* Fraud Analyst
* Case Management API (AWS ECS Fargate, Node.js/TypeScript)
* Case Controller, Case Workflow Service, Note & Tagging Service, Audit & Compliance Logger, Data Access Repository
* Amazon DynamoDB
* Amazon EventBridge
* WORM Compliance Storage (Amazon S3 with Object Lock Compliance mode)
* AWS Secrets Manager & AWS KMS

## Relationships
* Fraud Analyst -> Case Management API: Reviews cases and manages alerts [HTTPS/OAuth2/mTLS]
* Case Management API -> Amazon DynamoDB: Persists and retrieves active cases [TCP/AWS SDK]
* Case Management API -> Amazon EventBridge: Emits analyst tags and case annotations asynchronously [HTTPS/AWS SDK]
* Case Management API -> WORM Compliance Storage: Writes cryptographically signed audit payloads via AWS Lambda [HTTPS/AWS SDK]

## Technology Stack
* AWS ECS Fargate: Chosen for serverless container orchestration, minimizing operational overhead for a 3-person team.
* Node.js/TypeScript: Selected for rapid development of the Case Management API within the engineering team's expertise.
* Amazon DynamoDB: Provides low-latency, scalable NoSQL storage for active cases with strict PAN-masking.
* Amazon EventBridge: Enables decoupled, asynchronous event distribution for analyst tags and model feedback loops.
* AWS S3 WORM Storage: Utilizes S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode for tamper-evident, 7-year audit logging.
* AWS Secrets Manager & KMS: Enforces encryption at rest (AES-256) and dynamic credential rotation for PCI-DSS compliance.

## Rationale
[This architecture balances strict PCI-DSS security and 7-year auditability requirements with the operational constraints of a 3-person engineering team. By leveraging fully managed AWS services and asynchronous event-driven decoupling, it achieves high performance and reliability within the fixed 25,000 EUR monthly budget.]

Rule & Model Registry.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud to protect transactions while ensuring sub-50ms decision latency. It provides a secure, auditable, and highly available platform for payment processors, operating under PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance constraints.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts / Data Scientists / Fraud Managers (Users)
- AWS API Gateway / Application Load Balancer (ALB)
- Scoring Engine (AWS ECS Fargate / Go or Rust)
- Case Management API (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Rule & Model Registry (Registry API, Amazon S3, Amazon DynamoDB)
- External Systems: Payment Gateway/Acquirer, Tokenization Vault, Identity Provider (IdP), WORM Compliance Storage

## Relationships
- Scoring Engine -> Rule & Model Registry: Fetches versioned models and rules via HTTPS / AWS SigV4 with local in-memory caching.
- Registry API -> Amazon S3: Persists immutable binary model files and rule definitions (.onnx / .json) via AWS SDK.
- Registry API -> Amazon DynamoDB: Reads and writes version tags, access controls, and audit logs via AWS SDK.
- Fraud Analysts -> Case Management API: Reviews suspicious payments and manages cases via HTTPS.

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration for microservices, chosen for low operational overhead suitable for a three-engineer team.
- Amazon S3: Immutable binary artifact storage, selected for cost-efficiency within the 25k EUR/month budget.
- Amazon DynamoDB: Metadata and audit log storage with KMS encryption, providing low-latency tamper-evident tracking.
- AWS Lambda / Python FastAPI: Administrative REST interface for model uploads, schema validation, and RBAC.
- AWS KMS: Customer-managed encryption keys ensuring data protection at rest for PCI-DSS compliance.

Amazon DynamoDB.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening engine deployed on AWS eu-west-1, designed to score payment authorizations and manage fraud review cases. Its core purpose is to prevent fraudulent card-not-present transactions while maintaining a sub-50ms P99 decision latency at 3,000 TPS.]

## Key Elements
*   **Feature Store Table**: DynamoDB table managing operational feature data with automated TTL.
*   **Case Management Table**: DynamoDB table storing analyst review cases with DynamoDB Streams enabled.
*   **Idempotency Store Table**: DynamoDB table ensuring fail-open resilience under R-07.
*   **AWS KMS**: Provides Customer Managed Keys (CMKs) with annual key rotation for encryption at rest.
*   **AWS IAM**: Enforces least privilege using `dynamodb:LeadingKeys` condition keys and account-level SCPs.
*   **VPC Gateway Endpoints**: Secures private connectivity between ECS Fargate tasks and DynamoDB.
*   **Amazon Kinesis Data Streams**: Receives CDC events from DynamoDB Streams for downstream audit extraction.

## Relationships
*   **Scoring Engine -> Feature Store Table**: `Query/GetItem via AWS SDK (HTTPS)` over VPC Gateway Endpoints
*   **Case Management API -> Case Management Table**: `PutItem/UpdateItem via AWS SDK (HTTPS)` over VPC Gateway Endpoints
*   **Feature Store Table & Case Management Table -> DynamoDB Streams**: `Change Data Capture (CDC)` to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
*   **Scoring Engine & Case Management API -> AWS KMS**: `Decrypt/Encrypt via AWS SDK (HTTPS)` for tokenized and encrypted data

## Technology Stack
*   **Amazon DynamoDB**: Selected with On-Demand capacity to eliminate capacity planning toil for a 3-engineer team while supporting low-latency throughput.
*   **Terraform**: Utilized for Infrastructure as Code provisioning of all tables, TTLs, and KMS policies with drift detection.
*   **AWS CloudWatch & AWS Config**: Deployed for anomaly detection, Contributor Insights, and automated security rule compliance.

## Rationale
[This architecture fits requirements by leveraging serverless On-Demand DynamoDB components to meet stringent <50ms P99 latency constraints without exceeding the 25,000 EUR monthly budget or overwhelming a 3-engineer team. Strict encryption, VPC endpoints, and IAM guardrails ensure PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability.]

Amazon Kinesis Data Streams & AWS S3 Fir.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a real-time payment fraud screening engine that evaluates card-not-present transactions for a mid-size payment processor. Its core purpose is to score authorizations in under 50 milliseconds while routing suspicious cases to fraud analysts and maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.]

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer
- Fraud Screening Engine (Go / Rust, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management API (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Rule & Model Registry (Amazon S3)
- Amazon DynamoDB
- Amazon Kinesis Data Streams & AWS S3 Firehose
- Tokenization Vault
- Identity Provider (IdP)
- WORM Compliance Storage (Amazon S3 Object Lock)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer -> Fraud Screening Engine: Sends payment authorization requests [HTTPS / REST]
- Fraud Screening Engine -> Tokenization Vault: Tokenizes and retrieves card data [gRPC / HTTPS]
- Fraud Screening Engine -> Amazon DynamoDB: Reads/writes user profiles and case states [AWS SDK]
- Fraud Screening Engine -> Amazon Kinesis Data Streams: Streams audit logs [AWS SDK / HTTPS]
- Amazon Kinesis Data Streams -> Amazon S3 Firehose: Buffers and forwards records [AWS internal protocol]
- Amazon S3 Firehose -> WORM Compliance Storage: Persists immutable audit logs [AWS SDK / S3 API]
- Case Management API -> Amazon DynamoDB: Manages analyst review cases [AWS SDK]
- Fraud Analysts -> Case Management API: Reviews suspicious payments [HTTPS / Web]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Hosts containerized microservices without managing underlying servers, fitting the 3-engineer team constraint.
- Amazon Kinesis Data Streams & AWS S3 Firehose: Provides scalable real-time audit logging with built-in batching to control S3 storage costs.
- Amazon DynamoDB: Delivers predictable single-digit millisecond latency required for sub-50ms fraud decisions.
- Amazon S3 Object Lock: Ensures tamper-evident, 7-year regulatory audit retention required for PCI-DSS compliance.
- AWS PrivateLink: Secures internal transport of sensitive data across AWS components without traversing the public internet.

## Rationale
[This architecture strictly balances the 25,000 EUR monthly budget and 3-engineer operational limit through fully managed AWS serverless and container services. It guarantees sub-50ms performance and unbreakable PCI-DSS Level 1 auditability using isolated streaming and immutable storage.]
